asserts: Every refusal code a signal call can answer a person with has plain words in the trading rooms.

guard.ref: apps/customer/src/screens/trade/copybots/refusals.test.ts#maps every code the signal calls refuse with

why: Reads the refusals of the six market.signals records svc-market mounts (mountRecord), keeps the same code prefixes and the publisher's three internal codes out, and checks each against KNOWN_ROOM_CODES.

asserts: Every code svc-trade's copy service can refuse with has plain words in the trading rooms.
why: COPY_CODES satisfies Record<CopyErrorCode, true>, so the customer typecheck refuses a missing or stale code; the test checks every key against KNOWN_ROOM_CODES (all 101, the old read saw the 100 trade.copy_ ones).

asserts: Every code svc-trade's grid bots can refuse with, and the bot verification codes, have plain words in the trading rooms.
why: GRID_CODES satisfies Record<GridErrorCode, true>, so the customer typecheck refuses a missing or stale code; the test checks all 51 plus the four verification codes against KNOWN_ROOM_CODES (the old read saw only trade.grid_ and trade.bots_withdraw_).

asserts: The id the screen looks a newly created bot up by is the id svc-trade's engine stores it under.

guard.ref: apps/customer/src/screens/trade/copybots/guard.test.ts#prefixes a create with the first 8 of the user id, as svc-trade stores it

why: Runs TwapEngine.prepare (validates and builds the parent, stores nothing) for two users and asserts algoServiceId gives the minted id, keeps it on an operation, and never gives another user's id.

asserts: The console shows, for every order status, the word the customer's own API gives for it.

guard.ref: apps/admin/src/lib/trade-ops/order-read.test.ts#gives the customer’s own status word for every service status, as svc-trade’s customer API does

why: Calls svc-trade's toCcxtOrderStatus for every value of its order_status enum and asserts customerStatusOf answers the same; admin's test task now builds the three packages that module needs.

asserts: The console offers a kill for exactly the modules svc-edge routes to (permissions and kill switch).

guard.ref: apps/admin/src/lib/flag-state-edge.test.ts#names exactly the modules the edge routes to

why: Imports svc-edge's UPSTREAMS at run time and compares its module set with EDGE_PERIMETER_MODULES.
